correctness.rationale: For states Z/nZ, a is the forward n-cycle and b_j moves j-1 to j. Reverse preimages of a proper nonempty cyclic interval stay cyclic intervals: a shifts its left endpoint backward; b_j enlarges by one only when the old left endpoint equals j, then shifts that endpoint backward, or else remains stationary/shrinks. A reset-word inverse walk must have n-1 marked enlargement visits, producing the lower bound by the minimum cyclic scan length. Conversely each marked old endpoint can enlarge and each unmarked one can be shifted by a^-1, yielding a matching reset word after reversing the inverse-letter list. Decomposing n-1 visits into full tours gives the even/odd two-mark formulas and special n=2 boundary. An independently written forward subset BFS versus the scan formula exhaustively agrees for all 501 nonempty mark sets with 2<=n<=8. The finite BFS is supporting evidence only.
